also: what month were you born in?

terms.comment: The words and the construction are classical (the ablative of time with nātus, as in sī hic prīdiē nātus foret, Plaut. Mil. 4.2.91, Lewis & Short s.v. prīdiē), but we have found the question itself only in Traupman. The answer gives the day as an ordinal in the ablative: tertiō diē mēnsis Jānuāriī, on the third of January.

terms.gloss: what day (what month) were you born?

phrases.latin: Quō diē nāta es? — Quīntō diē mēnsis Majī.
phrases.english: What day were you born? — On the fifth of May.

sources: Lewis & Short: nascor · Lewis & Short: quando
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 74, 76.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
